findings.text: §20 says the harness counts the refused memo writes "by wrapping `_write_classification_memo` in `reckon/crew/recovery_memo.py` to count its calls", but the derivation's only call site bound that name at import (`from .recovery_memo import ... _write_classification_memo`, reckon/crew/recovery_classification.py:1612-1618, called at :1575), so patching the defining module intercepts no call and the harness logs zero however many memos the pass tries to write — and even a correctly targeted count counts calls, not refusals, because `_write_classification_memo` returns before its write when the run directory is absent or empty (reckon/crew/recovery_memo.py:190-195).

findings.reason: the node needs a content-level fingerprint of the per-run files the derivation reads (their mtimes and sizes, not their count), or the "same state" conclusion and the split resting on it have to be dropped.
findings.text: the changed done-when fingerprints the live tree with "live-pointer count and per-run file count" and keeps a pair whose fingerprint matches its copy's, concluding "both arms of a pair read the same state"; the plan's own next sentence rejects a stream mtime "because live workers write their streams every few seconds", yet the derivation reads exactly that stream state (`_run_stream_mtime(record)` at reckon/crew/recovery_classification.py:385, `_run_stream_quiet_seconds` at :82, `local_liveness` at :209), and an append changes neither the live-pointer count nor the per-run file count, so a pair whose streams moved is kept and its arm difference still carries corpus churn beside filesystem cost.
